LESSON: READING 7.4.1 CHARACTERS IN CLASS READERS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you tell the difference between a main and a minor character in a story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify minor characters in a text
2. discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text
3. appreciate the place of minor characters in the class reader

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 7.4.1 CHARACTERS IN CLASS READERS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 7.4.1 CHARACTERS IN CLASS READERS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify minor characters in a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify minor characters in a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify minor characters in a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify minor characters in a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the place of minor characters in the class reader

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the place of minor characters in the class reader. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the place of minor characters in the class reader.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the place of minor characters in the class reader. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify minor characters in a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers to a partner. (skill: discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the place of minor characters in the class reader)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify minor characters in a text.
3. Practise this skill: discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the place of minor characters in the class reader.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you tell the difference between a main and a minor character in a story?
2. How would you describe the behaviour of your classmates?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 7.4.1 Characters in Class Readers means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify minor characters in a text.
5. Be able to: discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the text.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
